title_en: Sanmenxia Water Conservancy Administration Bureau v. Zhengzhou Supporting Construction Company — dispute over a housing sales contract

full_text_en:
Sanmenxia Water Resources Administration v. Zhengzhou Supporting Construction Co., Ltd. — dispute over housing sale contract

Ruling Summary

The seller of a housing sale contract, after receiving most of the payment from the buyer, cannot refuse to deliver the house to the buyer as agreed in the contract on the ground that the construction cost of the house needs to be repaid with priority.

Plaintiff: Sanmenxia Water Control Project Administration of the Yellow River Water Resources Commission of the Ministry of Water Resources. Domicile: Xiaoshan Road, Sanmenxia City, Henan Province.

Legal Representative: Li Chun'an, Director of the Administration.

Defendant: Zhengzhou Supporting Construction Co., Ltd. Domicile: Shangfu New Village, Guancheng District, Zhengzhou City, Henan Province.

Legal Representative: Kang Jianxin, Chairman of the Company.

Plaintiff Sanmenxia Water Control Project Administration of the Yellow River Water Resources Commission of the Ministry of Water Resources (hereinafter referred to as the Water Resources Administration) filed a lawsuit with the Henan High People's Court due to a dispute over a housing sale contract with the defendant Zhengzhou Supporting Construction Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Supporting Construction Company).

Plaintiff alleged: The "Real Estate Transaction Contract" signed between our bureau and the defendant stipulated that Supporting Construction Company should deliver, by June 30, 1994, and no later than October 30, 1994, the property on the 1st to 13th floors of Block B of the Shangfu City commercial and residential building located on the northwest side of the intersection of West Street and Beixia Street in Zhengzhou City, with a total transaction amount of RMB 18,427,500, to be paid in installments. After the contract was signed, as of December 1993, our bureau had paid RMB 11,988,000 for the house purchase. The project is now substantially completed, but Supporting Construction Company has not delivered the property to date and has instead signed separate contracts for the sale of the same property with 24 persons including Zuo Kunpeng, constituting a breach of contract. The plaintiff requests that the court order the defendant to deliver the property as per the contract and pay liquidated damages and compensation for losses totaling RMB 23,576,200.

The plaintiff submitted evidence: the "Real Estate Transaction Contract" signed by both parties, supplementary agreement, transfer checks, payment vouchers, etc., to prove the performance after the effectiveness of the housing sale contract signed with the defendant.

The defendant argued: When our company signed the "Real Estate Transaction Contract" with the plaintiff, we had not obtained the state-owned land use certificate, building planning permit, construction permit, and pre-sale permit and other procedures required by laws and regulations for real estate development, construction, and transfer. Even at the expiration of the final performance deadline stipulated in the contract, we had not obtained all the statutory procedures, and no actual funds had been invested for development and construction. Therefore, the "Real Estate Transaction Contract" signed by both parties should be an invalid contract. The plaintiff knew that the contract was invalid but still signed it, so it was also at fault and should bear corresponding responsibility. The house involved in this case has been disposed of to a third party and relevant legal procedures have been completed, making it objectively impossible to deliver to the plaintiff. Therefore, the defendant requests that the contract be rescinded according to law, and both parties bear corresponding responsibilities.

The main evidence submitted by Supporting Construction Company:

1. The state-owned land use certificate, construction project planning permit, construction permit, and commercial housing pre-sale permit for this project were issued on July 9, 1996, October 20, 1993, December 14, 2000, and March 20, 2002, respectively, all after the contract was signed and before the first-instance trial of this case, to prove that it did not have the necessary legal procedures when the contract was signed.

2. Documents No. (1997)121 and No. (2002)370 of Zhengzhou Municipal Planning Commission, the construction project contract with Xingyang No.1 Construction, and the construction commencement notice, etc., to prove that when the contract was signed, not only were the procedures incomplete, but also no construction funds had actually been invested.

3. The "Supplementary Agreement on the Shangfu City Complex Building Project" signed by Supporting Construction Company and Xingyang No.1 Construction, to prove that Xingyang No.1 Construction used the property due to priority in compensation for the project price.

4. The "Commercial Housing Sale Contracts" signed by Supporting Construction Company with Zuo Kunpeng and 23 others, the mortgage business cooperation agreement with Huayuan Road Industrial and Commercial Bank, the "Individual Housing Loan Contracts", "Real Estate Mortgage Contracts", notarizations, and bank passbooks signed by Zuo Kunpeng and 21 others with Huayuan Road ICBC and Supporting Construction Company, to prove that the property has been sold to third parties.

During the examination and authentication of evidence in this case, both parties had no objection to the authenticity of the form of the evidence provided by the other party.

The Henan High People's Court found:

On December 27, 1992, the plaintiff Water Resources Administration and the defendant Supporting Construction Company signed four "Real Estate Transaction Contracts" and notarized them at the Zhengzhou Notary Public Office. The contract stipulated: the Water Resources Administration purchased from Supporting Construction Company the property on the 1st to 13th floors of Block B of the Shangfu City commercial and residential building located on the northwest side of the intersection of West Street and Beixia Street in Zhengzhou, with a total area of 5,441.26 square meters; the total transaction amount was RMB 18,427,500, to be paid in installments; the first installment was to be 40% of the contract price and was to serve as a deposit; the delivery deadline for the property was before June 30, 1994, and in no case later than October 31, 1994. If the Water Resources Administration delayed payment, it would pay a late fee of 1% of the amount due per month of delay; if delay exceeded two months, the contract would be deemed terminated, and Supporting Construction Company had the right to sell to another party with no refund of the deposit. If Supporting Construction Company failed to deliver the property for use within the specified period, unless due to force majeure, it would pay the Water Resources Administration a delay fee of 1% of the delayed portion per month; if delay exceeded two months, it would constitute a serious breach, and it should compensate the Water Resources Administration for economic losses equal to the full amount of the deposit. Any unilateral termination of the contract required the consent of the other party and compensation for losses equal to the full amount of the deposit. After the contract was signed, the Water Resources Administration paid the first installment of the four contracts in three installments on December 30, 1992, totaling RMB 7,360,000 as a deposit, and subsequently paid part of the house price in installments. As of December 1993, the Water Resources Administration had paid a total of RMB 11,987,900 to Supporting Construction Company. The project started in July 1992, but by the end of 1993, only the foundation work had been completed. Later, due to insufficient funds, the project was still unfinished by the final delivery deadline of October 31, 1994, as stipulated in the contract, and had been in a state of suspension ever since. On April 26, 2001, the project resumed construction, but it has not yet been completed. On October 29, 1993, the two parties reached a supplementary agreement on the progress of the project and the third installment payment, stipulating that payment would be made according to the project progress. Before this lawsuit, Supporting Construction Company had not delivered the house to the Water Resources Administration, and the Water Resources Administration still had RMB 6,439,500 in unpaid house purchase price.

It was also found that when Supporting Construction Company signed the four "Real Estate Transaction Contracts" with the Water Resources Administration, it had not yet obtained the land use right certificate, building planning permit, construction permit, and pre-sale permit and other relevant procedures for the development property. On March 20, 2002, the Zhengzhou Land Administration Bureau issued the commercial housing pre-sale permit for the Shangfu City Complex Building to Supporting Construction Company. On January 10, 2001, Supporting Construction Company and Xingyang No.1 Construction signed a supplementary agreement for the Shangfu City Complex Building, stipulating that if Supporting Construction Company failed to pay the project funds as agreed, Xingyang No.1 Construction had the right to use the part below the fifth floor after decoration according to the original design but with reduced standards, until the principal and interest were recovered or Supporting Construction Company paid the project funds, then Xingyang No.1 Construction would return that part. Later, due to arrears in project funds, Xingyang No.1 Construction actually occupied the first to third floors of Block B of the property, totaling 1,437 square meters. The fourth to thirteenth floors of Block B had been sold in 24 units, and the housing transaction contracts were all registered and filed with the Zhengzhou Real Estate Management Office. Of the 24 units sold, 20 were sold from October 31 to December 6, 2001, and 4 were sold from March to April 2002. Among them, 21 buyers purchased through bank mortgages and went through mortgage registration procedures with the Zhengzhou Real Estate Administration Bureau. These 24 units have not been delivered to date, and the property title transfer registration procedures have not been completed. The 24 buyers have not obtained the property ownership certificates. Supporting Construction Company acknowledged that among the 21 mortgage buyers, there were Li Bing, the deputy general manager of the company, and Kang Ping, the sister of Kang Jie, the deputy general manager. Before the lawsuit, the Water Resources Administration applied to the Henan High People's Court for pre-litigation property preservation. On March 6, 2002, the Henan High People's Court issued Civil Ruling No. (2002) Yufa Limin Bao Zi No. 2, freezing Supporting Construction Company's deposits of RMB 35,564,200 or sealing up 5,441.26 square meters of the company's property.

The Henan High People's Court held:

This case is a dispute over a commercial housing sale contract. The main issues in dispute between the parties are: (1) the validity of the contract and allocation of liability; (2) whether the contract can be performed continuously. Since the housing sale contract between the parties was signed before the implementation of the "Urban Real Estate Administration Law of the People's Republic of China" (hereinafter referred to as the Real Estate Administration Law), the "General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China" and the Supreme People's Court's "Interpretations on Several Issues concerning the Trial of Cases Involving Real Estate Development and Operations before the Implementation of the Real Estate Administration Law" (hereinafter referred to as the "Interpretations") shall apply.

Article 25 of the Interpretations stipulates: "If the preseller of commercial housing has not obtained the land use certificate, but has invested a certain amount of development and construction funds and carried out construction, and if during the first-instance trial the land use certificate and commercial housing pre-sale permit are obtained retroactively, the pre-sale contract may be deemed valid." In this case, the four "Real Estate Transaction Contracts" signed by the plaintiff Water Resources Administration and the defendant Supporting Construction Company on December 27, 1992, and the supplementary agreement reached on October 29, 1993, were all true expressions of the parties' intent and did not violate any prohibitive provisions of national laws or regulations. Although when the contract was signed, Supporting Construction Company had not yet obtained the land use certificate and other relevant procedures, before the case was litigated, it had invested a certain amount of development and construction funds, carried out construction, and obtained the land use certificate and handled the relevant development, construction, and pre-sale procedures. Therefore, the pre-sale contract signed by both parties should be a valid contract. Supporting Construction Company's argument that the contract between the parties was invalid does not conform to the relevant judicial interpretations, so it is not accepted.

After the contract was signed, the Water Resources Administration paid most of the house purchase price to Supporting Construction Company in accordance with the contract, fulfilling its obligations under the contract. However, Supporting Construction Company not only failed to deliver the property on time as agreed, but also unilaterally disposed of the relevant property by selling it to others or handing it over to the construction party for possession and use, using the proceeds to offset overdue project funds with priority. Supporting Construction Company's actions violated the contract with the Water Resources Administration and seriously infringed on the legitimate rights and interests of the Water Resources Administration, for which it should bear liability for breach of contract. Supporting Construction Company's claim that the contract with the Water Resources Administration was invalid and that the Water Resources Administration was also at fault and should bear corresponding responsibility lacks factual and legal basis and is not supported.

On the issue of whether the contract can continue to be performed:

Article 27 of the Interpretations stipulates: "After a pre-sale contract for commercial housing is signed, if the preseller, without the consent of the buyer, enters into another pre-sale contract with a third party for the same pre-sold property before the buyer obtains the property ownership certificate, the later pre-sale contract shall be deemed invalid; if the buyer under the later contract has already obtained the property ownership certificate, the later contract may be deemed valid, but the preseller shall bear corresponding civil liability for the losses caused to the buyer under the earlier contract." In this case, the contract between Supporting Construction Company and the Water Resources Administration was signed first, while the housing sale contracts with Zuo Kunpeng and 23 others were signed later. Although the properties purchased by Zuo Kunpeng and 23 others have been registered with the property management department, the properties have not been delivered, and they have not actually obtained the property ownership certificates. Therefore, Supporting Construction Company's sale of the properties to Zuo Kunpeng and 23 others cannot oppose the rights of the Water Resources Administration as the house buyer.

Furthermore, although Xingyang No.1 Construction occupies part of the property due to its priority right to compensation for the project price, it has not actually obtained ownership. The rights it obtained through the contract with Supporting Construction Company are only the rights to possess, use, and benefit from the house, which cannot oppose the rights enjoyed by the Water Resources Administration. In addition, the house has not yet been completed and delivered for use, and the rights of Xingyang No.1 Construction and the 24 buyers including Zuo Kunpeng can also be protected through other means.

Supporting Construction Company, as the seller of the housing sale contract, after receiving most of the payment from the buyer, cannot refuse to deliver the house to the buyer as agreed in the contract on the ground that the construction cost of the house needs to be repaid with priority. Therefore, the litigation claims of the Water Resources Administration should be supported.

Based on the contract terms and the principles of good faith and fairness, Supporting Construction Company should compensate the Water Resources Administration for economic losses equal to the full amount of the deposit. According to the contract terms, if Supporting Construction Company delayed delivery of the house for more than two months, it should compensate the Water Resources Administration for losses equal to the deposit, i.e., RMB 7,360,000. Since the Water Resources Administration still has RMB 6,439,500 in unpaid house purchase price, this amount can be offset against the compensation paid by Supporting Construction Company.

Supporting Construction Company's argument that the house has been disposed of to a third party and the contract cannot be performed continuously does not comply with legal provisions and is not accepted.

Accordingly, in accordance with Article 4 of the "General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China" and Articles 25 and 27 of the Supreme People's Court's "Interpretations on Several Issues concerning the Trial of Cases Involving Real Estate Development and Operations before the Implementation of the Real Estate Administration Law", the Henan High People's Court rendered the following judgment on July 26, 2003:

1. The real estate transaction contract and supplementary agreement for the Shangfu City Complex Building signed between the Sanmenxia Water Control Project Administration of the Yellow River Water Resources Commission of the Ministry of Water Resources and Zhengzhou Supporting Construction Co., Ltd. are legal and valid and shall continue to be performed;

2. Zhengzhou Supporting Construction Co., Ltd. shall deliver the property as stipulated in the contract to the Sanmenxia Water Control Project Administration of the Yellow River Water Resources Commission of the Ministry of Water Resources within sixty days after this judgment takes effect;

3. Zhengzhou Supporting Construction Co., Ltd. shall pay liquidated damages of RMB 7,360,000 to the Sanmenxia Water Control Project Administration of the Yellow River Water Resources Commission of the Ministry of Water Resources within ten days after this judgment takes effect, and the Sanmenxia Water Control Project Administration of the Yellow River Water Resources Commission of the Ministry of Water Resources shall pay RMB 6,439,500 in house purchase price to Zhengzhou Supporting Construction Co., Ltd.; after offsetting the above payments, Zhengzhou Supporting Construction Co., Ltd. shall pay RMB 920,500 to the Sanmenxia Water Control Project Administration of the Yellow River Water Resources Commission of the Ministry of Water Resources within ten days after this judgment takes effect; in case of delay, payment shall be made at double the interest on the debt for the period of delayed performance.

Court acceptance fee of RMB 187,831 and property preservation fee of RMB 178,350, totaling RMB 366,181, shall be borne by Zhengzhou Supporting Construction Co., Ltd.

After the judgment was pronounced, Supporting Construction Company filed an appeal with the Supreme People's Court, but later applied for withdrawal of the appeal on the ground that an out-of-court settlement was expected.

The Supreme People's Court, upon review, held that Supporting Construction Company's application for withdrawal of the appeal was a genuine expression of intent and did not violate legal provisions. In accordance with Article 156 of the "Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China" and Article 23, Paragraph 1 of the "Measures for Litigation Costs of the People's Courts", the court ruled on March 11, 2004:

Zhengzhou Supporting Construction Co., Ltd. is permitted to withdraw its appeal.

The court acceptance fee for the second instance of RMB 93,915.5 shall be borne by Zhengzhou Supporting Construction Co., Ltd.
